experiments.purpose: Prospectively test whether response remembers the oldest drive versus recent drive, at fixed current drive and wait.
Paired order contrast against oldest-drive pulse at same current drive and wait.
Test whether the oldest-drive effect decays with waiting time.
Test recent-drive response at longer wait against the paired old-pulse condition.

prospective_contrast: At fixed u=0.3, h=0.5, compare [1,0,0,0] with [0,0,0,1]; model predicts equal response because both histories have the same mean. A reproducible difference exceeding the combined 0.03 response-unit error bound refutes this mean-memory model. Existing data already indicate such a difference, so this is a targeted falsification contrast, not claimed confirmation.

quantities.interpretation: Mean of the four prior dimensionless drive intervals; candidate summary of integrated drive history.
quantities.name: memory

refutation_condition: Reject this response if held-out dev RMSE exceeds 0.06, or if a prospective equal-mean history-order contrast differs by more than 0.03 response units under the stated measurement bound.
scientific_change: Replace the assumption that current drive and waiting time alone determine response with a candidate additive dependence on the mean of prior drive. This is intentionally a simple testable summary; the observed A/B and fresh paired histories suggest order may matter, so a failed dev fit or prospective order contrast should motivate a time-weighted/history-order representation.
